# score { #falconage.score }

`score`

The scoring loop and its result object.

| [FalconResult](#falconage.score.FalconResult) | Scores plus everything needed to say where they came from. |

### FalconResult { #falconage.score.FalconResult }

```python
score.FalconResult(
    scores,
    obs,
    manifest,
    registry,
    coverage=dict(),
    skipped=dict(),
)
```

Scores plus everything needed to say where they came from.

``scores`` is samples x clocks. Everything else -- coverage, warnings,
weight digests, the resolved config -- hangs off the manifest, so a result
written to disk and read back is self-describing.

##### long { #falconage.score.FalconResult.long }

```python
score.FalconResult.long()
```

One row per sample per clock, with the scale and provenance attached.

The scale column is not decoration: it is what stops a reader averaging
a mortality log-hazard with an age in years because both were numbers in
a column called ``value``.

### combine { #falconage.score.combine }

```python
score.combine(results, *, keys=None, dataset_col='dataset')
```

Stack per-dataset results into one, for a benchmark across studies.

Datasets are scored separately and combined afterwards, never merged before
scoring. Two reasons, and the second is the one that bites:

* a 27K study and an EPIC study have different probe spaces, and the outer
  join of ten of them is a mostly-NaN matrix that no clock should see;
* feature coverage is a property of a dataset. Merged, a clock that covers
  99% of one study and 40% of another reports a single meaningless average,
  and the AA2 test silently compares cases in the well-covered study against
  controls in the badly-covered one.

Per-clock coverage is kept per dataset in ``uns`` and the manifests are
merged, so a combined result still says which study contributed what.

### score { #falconage.score.score }

```python
score.score(
    data,
    clocks='compatible',
    *,
    device='auto',
    dtype=None,
    imputation='reference',
    min_coverage=0.8,
    reference=None,
    registry=None,
    caller='python',
)
```

Score a dataset against one or more clocks.

#### Parameters {.doc-section .doc-section-parameters}

| Name         | Type                                                          | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  | Default        |
|--------------|---------------------------------------------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|----------------|
| clocks       | [str](`str`) \| [Sequence](`typing.Sequence`)\[[str](`str`)\] | ``"compatible"`` scores everything this dataset can support and reports the rest as skipped with a reason. ``"all"`` attempts every clock of the right modality and fails loudly on the ones that cannot run. A list names them explicitly, and every name in it must work -- an explicit request is never silently dropped. | `'compatible'` |
| imputation   | [str](`str`)                                                  | Passed to the per-clock feature alignment. See :func:`falconage.models.linear.align`; the short version is that zero is never a fill value.                                                                                                                                                                                  | `'reference'`  |
| min_coverage | [float](`float`)                                              | The fraction of a clock's features that must be present. Below it, the clock is skipped (``clocks="compatible"``) or raises (explicit list).                                                                                                                                                                                 | `0.8`          |
| reference    |                                                               | A fitted :class:`~falconage.models.clinical.KDMReference` or :class:`~falconage.models.clinical.HDReference`, for the two clinical clocks that have no fixed coefficients.                                                                                                                                                   | `None`         |

#### Returns {.doc-section .doc-section-returns}

| Name   | Type                                           | Description                                                                                                             |
|--------|------------------------------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
|        | [FalconResult](`falconage.score.FalconResult`) | Scores, per-clock coverage, and a manifest recording the device, the dtype, every coefficient digest and every warning. |
